This comparison details the types of re-operations performed on patients with [[ibd|IBD]] (Indicator 6), as recorded by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] [^src1]. The data breaks down 14 distinct surgical procedure codes by their frequency and percentage of the total re-operations [^src1].

The most frequently performed re-operations are endoscopic dilation of the large intestine (KJFA58 - Endoskopisk dilatation af tyktarm) and small intestine resection (KJFB00 - Tyndtarmsresektion) [^src1]. Both of these procedures tie for the leading position, with 6 occurrences each, accounting for 21.4% of the total re-operations [^src1]. The third most common procedure is loop enterostomy (KJFF10 - Loop enterostomi), which was performed 4 times, representing 14.3% of the cases [^src1].

The remaining 11 procedure types represent the lowest frequencies, with their exact counts suppressed and marked with a '#' symbol to protect patient anonymity when numbers are very low [^src1]. Among these trailing categories, other intestinal resection (KJFB96 - Anden tarmresektion) accounts for 7.1% of the total [^src1]. The final 10 procedures each account for 3.6% of the total re-operations [^src1]. These less common interventions include endoscopic dilations of the small intestine, ileocecal resections, colectomies with ileostomy, and enteroenterostomies [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends or changes over time can be established [^src1]. Furthermore, the data does not specify any clinical targets or thresholds for these re-operation rates [^src1].

Beyond this specific indicator, the broader context of IBD patient demographics, medical treatments, and other quality metrics is extensively documented across the 2023 and 2024 annual reports [^src3] [^src4] [^src6] [^src7]. Additional sections of these publications provide comprehensive overviews of surgical outcomes, regional variations, and overall database performance [^src2] [^src5] [^src8].
